name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz largely shut; mine claims 4 Nov
summary: Hormuz largely shut; IRGC claims four tankers hit mines; Houthis claim strikes on Saudi Arabia
state: The IRGC said on 4 Nov that four tankers hit mines in a prohibited lane south of Hormuz and that it detained two vessels; the claims could not be independently verified (Al Jazeera). UKMTO reported two projectiles hit a tanker's engine room off Limah, Oman, on 3 Nov (Arab Times). Iran ties reopening the strait to sanctions relief and an end to the US naval blockade. The Houthis claimed missile attacks on Saudi targets on 4 Nov (AP).
for_you: Shipping through the Gulf faces severe disruption. Mariners should follow UKMTO and flag-state advisories; travellers should check FCDO travel advice for the region.

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Iran says US reply to Hormuz plan 'unconvincing'; Trump confirms strikes
Arab Times — UKMTO reports vessel hit, Iran claims tankers hit mines
AP via KRMG — Iranians celebrate setback for Trump in US election, and other Mideast news

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
